peer_risks.name: Inability to obtain necessary IP licenses
peer_risks.why: Licenses may not be available, or if available, could require significant royalty payments; alternative non-infringing solutions may be impossible or too expensive to develop.
peer_risks.description: May be unable to obtain licenses for required intellectual property on commercially reasonable terms, or at all, forcing costly alternatives or business disruption.

peer_risks.source_text:
The results of litigation
and claims to which we may be subject cannot be predicted with certainty. Even if these matters do not result in litigation or are resolved
in our favor or without significant cash settlements, these matters, and the time and resources necessary to litigate or resolve them,
could harm our business, reputation and operating results.
peer_risks.name: Litigation uncertainty and resource drain
peer_risks.why: Litigation outcomes are unpredictable, and even non-monetary resolutions require significant time and resources that divert focus from operations.
peer_risks.description: Legal disputes, even if resolved favorably, may harm business, reputation, and operating results due to time and resource consumption.

peer_risks.source_text:
We use open-source software
that we have obtained from third parties or is included in software packages in our solutions and will continue to use open source software
in the future. Open-source software is generally freely accessible, usable and modifiable, and is made available to the general public
on an “as-is” basis under the terms of a non-negotiable license. From time to time, we may face claims from third parties
claiming ownership of, or demanding release of, the open source software and/or derivative works that we developed using such software
(which could include our proprietary source code), or otherwise seeking to enforce the terms of the applicable open source license. These
claims could result in litigation and could require us to purchase a costly license or cease offering the implicated solutions unless
and until we can re-engineer them to avoid infringement. This re-engineering process could require significant additional research and
development resources. In addition to risks related to license requirements, use of certain open-source software can lead to greater risks
than use of third party commercial software, as open source licensors generally do not provide warranties or controls on the origin of
software. Any of these risks could be difficult to eliminate or manage, and, if not addressed, could have a negative effect on our business
and operating results.
peer_risks.name: Open-source license compliance risks
peer_risks.why: Third parties may claim ownership of open-source derivatives or demand compliance, forcing costly licensing, cessation of offerings, or re-engineering with significant R&D effort.
peer_risks.description: Use of open-source software may trigger claims demanding release of proprietary code or enforcement of license terms, leading to litigation or forced changes.

peer_risks.source_text:
Our business depends on our
intellectual property, the protection of which is crucial to the success of our business. We rely on a combination of trademark, trade
secret and other intellectual property rights and laws and contractual restrictions to protect our intellectual property. As examples
of such restrictions, we attempt to protect our intellectual property, technology and confidential information by entering into confidentiality
and inventions assignment agreements and non-competition agreements with employees, contractors, consultants and business partners who
develop intellectual property on our behalf, and entering into non-disclosure agreements with our business partners. These agreements
may not effectively prevent unauthorized use or disclosure of our confidential information, intellectual property or technology and may
not provide an adequate remedy in the event of unauthorized use or disclosure of our confidential information, intellectual property or
technology. Despite our efforts to protect our proprietary rights, unauthorized parties, as examples, may copy aspects of our website
features, software and functionality or obtain and use information that we consider proprietary.
peer_risks.name: Inadequate protection of proprietary IP
peer_risks.why: Confidentiality and assignment agreements may not effectively prevent copying of website features, software, or proprietary information, and may not provide adequate legal remedies.
peer_risks.description: Contractual and legal measures to protect trade secrets and proprietary technology may fail to prevent unauthorized use or disclosure.

peer_risks.source_text:
Despite our efforts to protect
our intellectual property rights, including trademarks, they may not be recognized in the future, or may be invalidated, circumvented
or challenged. For example, we have registered, among numerous other trademarks, “SpringBig” as a trademark in the U.S. Competitors
have and may continue to adopt service names similar to ours, thereby harming our ability to build brand identity and possibly leading
to consumer confusion. In addition, there could be potential trade name or trademark infringement claims brought by owners of other trademarks
that are similar to our trademarks. Litigation or proceedings before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office or other governmental authorities
and administrative bodies in the U.S. and abroad may be necessary in the future to enforce our intellectual property rights and to determine
the validity and scope of the proprietary rights of others. Our efforts to enforce or protect our proprietary rights may be ineffective
and could result in substantial costs and diversion of resources, which could harm our business and operating results.
peer_risks.name: Intellectual property rights may not be recognized, invalidated, circumvented, or challenged
peer_risks.why: Competitors have adopted and may continue to adopt similar service names, leading to brand confusion and potential litigation, which could incur substantial costs and divert resources.
peer_risks.description: SpringBig's trademarks, including 'SpringBig', may be challenged, infringed upon, or invalidated by competitors or third parties.

peer_risks.source_text:
Further, we may be subject,
from time-to-time, to claims that former employees, collaborators or other third parties have an interest in our intellectual property
as an inventor or co-inventor. We generally enter into confidentiality and intellectual property assignment agreements with our employees,
consultants, and contractors. These agreements generally provide that inventions conceived by the party in the course of rendering services
to us will be our exclusive property. However, those agreements may not be honored and may not effectively assign intellectual property
rights to us. Moreover, there may be some circumstances, where we are unable to negotiate for such ownership rights. If we are subject
to a dispute challenging our rights in or to patents or other intellectual property, such a dispute could be expensive and time consuming.
If we were unsuccessful, we could lose valuable rights in intellectual property that we regard as our own, which could have a material
adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects.
peer_risks.name: Disputes over ownership of intellectual property by former employees or third parties
peer_risks.why: Despite confidentiality and assignment agreements, these may not be honored or effectively assign rights, and in some cases ownership rights could not be negotiated, risking loss of valuable IP.
peer_risks.description: SpringBig may face claims that former employees or collaborators have ownership rights in its intellectual property.

peer_risks.source_text:
Our common stock is
quoted on the OTCQX® Best Market, a trading platform of OTC Markets Group, instead of a national exchange or quotation system. Accordingly,
our investors may experience significant volatility in the market price of our stock and have difficulty selling their shares.
peer_risks.name: Stock trading on OTCQX® leads to volatility and difficulty selling shares
peer_risks.why: OTC trading is characterized by lack of price quotations, inconsistent supervision, lower volume, and sporadic trading, leading to wide price fluctuations unrelated to performance.
peer_risks.description: SpringBig's stock trades on OTCQX®, which has thin trading volume and high price volatility, making it hard for investors to sell shares.

peer_risks.source_text:
Our common stock is currently
quoted on the OTCQX® Best Market, a trading platform of OTC Markets Group, under the ticker symbol “SBIG.” The OTC Markets
Group is a regulated quotation service that displays real-time quotes, last sale prices, and volume limitations in over-the-counter securities.
Trading in shares quoted on an OTC Markets Group trading platform is often thin and characterized by volatility in trading prices. This
volatility may be caused by a variety of factors, including the lack of readily available price quotations, the absence of consistent
administrative supervision of bid and ask quotations, lower trading volume, and market conditions. As a result, there may be wide fluctuations
in the market price of the shares of our Common Stock for reasons unrelated to operating performance, and this volatility, when it occurs,
may have a negative effect on the market price for our securities. Moreover, the OTC Markets Group is not a national stock exchange, and
trading of securities on one of its trading platforms is often more sporadic than the trading of securities listed on a national quotation
system or stock exchange. Accordingly, our stockholders may not be able to realize a fair price from their securities when they determine
to sell them or may have to hold them for a substantial period of time until the market for our common stock improves, and as a result
of our quotation for trading on the OTCQX® Best Market, we may be negatively impacted in our ability to raise equity financing, be
limited in our ability to issue additional securities or obtain additional financing in the future, and may face negative impacts on our
reputation and, consequently, our business.
peer_risks.name: Stock trading on OTCQX® hampers ability to raise capital and damages reputation
peer_risks.why: OTCQX® is not a national exchange, and trading is more sporadic, limiting access to financing, restricting future securities issuance, and negatively affecting business reputation.
peer_risks.description: Trading on OTCQX® negatively impacts SpringBig’s ability to raise equity financing and issue securities, and harms its reputation.

peer_risks.source_text:
If our performance does not
meet market expectations, the price of our shares of common stock may decline. In addition, even if an active market for our shares of
common stock develops and continues, the trading price of our shares of common stock could be volatile and subject to wide fluctuations
in response to various factors, some of which are beyond our control. Any of the factors listed below could have a material adverse effect
on the price of our shares of common stock.
peer_risks.name: Stock price may decline if performance fails to meet market expectations
peer_risks.why: Market expectations drive stock price movements, and failure to meet them can directly cause a decline in share price, regardless of underlying fundamentals.
peer_risks.description: SpringBig's stock price may fall if its performance does not meet market expectations.

peer_risks.source_text:
●
sales of substantial amounts of our shares of common stock by the Company,
the Investors or our directors, executive officers or significant shareholders or the perception that such sales could occur; and
peer_risks.name: Sales of substantial amounts of shares may depress stock price
peer_risks.why: Sales by the Company, investors, directors, executive officers, or significant shareholders — or even the perception of such sales — can negatively impact market price.
peer_risks.description: Large sales of SpringBig's shares by insiders or major shareholders may cause the stock price to decline.

peer_risks.source_text:
Broad market and industry
factors may depress the market price of our shares of common stock irrespective of our operating performance. The stock market in general
has experienced price and volume fluctuations that have often been unrelated or disproportionate to the operating performance of the particular
companies affected. The trading prices and valuations of these shares, and of our securities, may not be predictable. A loss of investor
confidence in the market for companies engaging in digital payments or the shares of other companies which investors perceive to be similar
to us could depress our stock price regardless of our business, prospects, financial conditions or results of operations. A decline in
the market price of our shares of common stock also could adversely affect our ability to issue additional securities and our ability
to obtain additional financing in the future.
peer_risks.name: Broad market and industry factors may depress stock price irrespective of performance
peer_risks.why: Stock market fluctuations are often unrelated to company performance, and investor confidence in similar companies or the digital payments industry can directly affect SpringBig's valuation.
peer_risks.description: Market-wide volatility or loss of investor confidence in digital payments sector may depress SpringBig's stock price regardless of its performance.

peer_risks.source_text:
Because there are no
current plans to pay cash dividends on our shares of common stock for the foreseeable future, you may not receive any return on investment
unless you sell our shares of common stock for a price greater than that which you paid for it; furthermore, there is no guarantee that
the value of the shares of common stock will increase to a price greater than that which you paid for it.
peer_risks.name: No cash dividends planned
peer_risks.why: The company states it will retain future earnings for operations, expansion, and debt repayment, and any future dividend decisions are at the Board’s discretion, subject to financial condition and contractual restrictions.
peer_risks.description: The company has no current plans to pay cash dividends, so investors may not receive any return unless they sell shares at a higher price.

peer_risks.source_text:
Because there are no
current plans to pay cash dividends on our shares of common stock for the foreseeable future, you may not receive any return on investment
unless you sell our shares of common stock for a price greater than that which you paid for it; furthermore, there is no guarantee that
the value of the shares of common stock will increase to a price greater than that which you paid for it.
peer_risks.name: No guarantee of stock price appreciation
peer_risks.why: Multiple paragraphs (0, 1, 8) explicitly state there is no guarantee the stock price will rise above the purchase price, even if dividends are not paid.
peer_risks.description: There is no guarantee that the value of the common stock will increase above the purchase price, leaving investors with no return unless they sell at a profit.

peer_risks.source_text:
The market price of our common
stock may be volatile and, in the past, companies that have experienced volatility in the market price of their stock have been subject
to securities class action litigation. We may be the target of this type of litigation in the future. Securities litigation against us
could result in substantial costs and divert management’s attention from other business concerns, which could seriously harm our
business.
peer_risks.name: Stock price volatility may trigger securities litigation
peer_risks.why: Paragraph [2] states that companies with volatile stock prices have been subject to such litigation, and SpringBig may be targeted, risking costs and distraction.
peer_risks.description: Volatility in the stock price could lead to securities class action litigation, which could incur substantial costs and divert management attention.

peer_risks.source_text:
The issuance of our
shares of common stock in connection with the Convertible Notes or that may otherwise be issued and/or sold by the Company or selling
securityholders, could cause substantial dilution, which could materially affect the trading price of our shares of common stock.
peer_risks.name: Dilution from convertible note conversions
peer_risks.why: Paragraphs [3] and [4] state that issuances from convertible note conversions could result in substantial dilution and materially affect or decrease the trading price.
peer_risks.description: Conversion of convertible notes into common stock could cause substantial dilution, materially affecting the stock price.

peer_risks.source_text:
A significant portion
of our total outstanding shares may be sold into the market at any time. This could cause the market price of our shares of common stock
to drop significantly, even if our business is doing well.
peer_risks.name: Large volume of shares available for sale
peer_risks.why: Paragraphs [5], [6], [7], [8], and [9] repeatedly state that large volumes of shares may be sold due to registration rights, warrants, equity plans, or resales by major holders.
peer_risks.description: A significant portion of outstanding shares may be sold at any time, potentially causing the stock price to drop significantly.

peer_risks.source_text:
Sales of a substantial number
of shares of common stock in the public market could occur at any time as a result of issuances and resales of shares of common stock
including shares subject to the Convertible Notes and our public and private warrants, as well as the resale of shares of common stock
by other holders, and pursuant to the Company’s equity incentive plan. These sales, or the perception in the market that the holders
of a large number of shares intend to sell shares, could reduce the market price of our shares of common stock.
peer_risks.name: Perception of large-scale sales may depress stock price
peer_risks.why: Paragraphs [6], [7], [8], and [9] explicitly state that the perception of intended sales, not just actual sales, could reduce the market price.
peer_risks.description: The perception that major shareholders intend to sell large numbers of shares could reduce the market price, even if no sales occur.

peer_risks.source_text:
The sale of our shares of
common stock in the public market or otherwise, or the perception that such sales could occur, could harm the prevailing market price
of our shares of common stock. These sales, or the possibility that these sales may occur, also might make it more difficult for us to
sell equity securities in the future at a time and at a price that it deems appropriate. Institutional investors and our founder that
collectively beneficially own in excess of 50% of the Company’s outstanding shares in the aggregate will be able to resell their
shares for so long as a registration statement is available for use. Resales of our shares of common stock may cause the market price
of our securities to drop significantly, regardless of the performance of our business.
peer_risks.name: Resales by large shareholders may depress price
peer_risks.why: Paragraph [8] states that these shareholders can resell shares while a registration statement is available, and such resales may cause price drops regardless of business performance.
peer_risks.description: Resales by institutional investors and founders who own over 50% of shares could significantly drop the stock price regardless of business performance.

peer_risks.source_text:
We have filed registration
statements relating to the resale of a large number of shares of common stock representing a large percentage of our public float pursuant
to securities held by certain existing shareholders for which such securityholders have registration rights. As such, sales of a substantial
number of shares of common stock in the public market could occur at any time. Given the substantial number of shares of common stock
being registered for potential resale or the perception in the market that the stockholders of a large number of shares intend to sell
shares, could increase the volatility of the market price of our common stock or result in a significant decline in the public trading
price of our common stock. Further, certain shares of our common stock that are being registered for resale include shares that were purchased
at prices that may be significantly below the trading price of our shares of common stock and the sale of which would result in such selling
securityholders realizing a significant gain. Even if our trading price remains low, certain selling securityholders may still have an
incentive to sell shares of our common stock because they purchased the shares at prices lower than the public investors or the current
trading price of our common stock. Public holders of our shares of common stock may not experience a similar rate of return on their shares.
peer_risks.name: Registered resale shares may increase volatility or cause price decline
peer_risks.why: Paragraph [9] states that registered shares represent a large percentage of public float, and their potential sale or perception of sale could increase volatility or cause price decline.
peer_risks.description: Registration of a large number of shares for resale may increase volatility or cause a significant decline in the trading price of common stock.

peer_risks.source_text:
We have filed registration
statements relating to the resale of a large number of shares of common stock representing a large percentage of our public float pursuant
to securities held by certain existing shareholders for which such securityholders have registration rights. As such, sales of a substantial
number of shares of common stock in the public market could occur at any time. Given the substantial number of shares of common stock
being registered for potential resale or the perception in the market that the stockholders of a large number of shares intend to sell
shares, could increase the volatility of the market price of our common stock or result in a significant decline in the public trading
price of our common stock. Further, certain shares of our common stock that are being registered for resale include shares that were purchased
at prices that may be significantly below the trading price of our shares of common stock and the sale of which would result in such selling

incentive to sell shares of our common stock because they purchased the shares at prices lower than the public investors or the current

peer_risks.name: Incentive for early investors to sell at a gain
peer_risks.why: Paragraph [9] notes that some registered shares were purchased at prices significantly below current trading prices, giving those holders incentive to sell for profit.
peer_risks.description: Early investors who bought shares at lower prices may sell despite low trading prices, realizing gains that public investors may not experience.

peer_risks.source_text:
The sale of our shares of
common stock in the public market or otherwise, or the perception that such sales could occur, could harm the prevailing market price
of our shares of common stock. These sales, or the possibility that these sales may occur, also might make it more difficult for us to
sell equity securities in the future at a time and at a price that it deems appropriate. Institutional investors and our founder that
collectively beneficially own in excess of 50% of the Company’s outstanding shares in the aggregate will be able to resell their
shares for so long as a registration statement is available for use. Resales of our shares of common stock may cause the market price
of our securities to drop significantly, regardless of the performance of our business.
peer_risks.name: Difficulty raising future equity capital
peer_risks.why: Paragraph [8] explicitly states that such sales or the possibility of them may make it more difficult to sell equity securities at a time and price deemed appropriate.
peer_risks.description: Sales or perceived sales of shares may make it harder to sell equity securities in the future at desirable times or prices.

peer_risks.source_text:
If securities or industry
analysts do not publish or cease publishing research or reports about us, our business, or our market, or if they change their recommendations
regarding our common stock adversely, the price and trading volume of our common stock could decline.
peer_risks.name: Loss of analyst coverage or adverse recommendations
peer_risks.why: The trading market for the stock is influenced by analyst reports; adverse recommendations or cessation of coverage reduces visibility and can cause price or volume decline, as stated in paragraphs [0] and [1].
peer_risks.description: If analysts stop covering SpringBig or issue negative recommendations, stock price and trading volume may decline.

peer_risks.source_text:
We may amend the terms
of our public warrants in a manner that may be adverse to holders with the approval by the holders of at least 65% of then outstanding
public warrants. As a result, the exercise price of your warrants could be increased, the exercise period could be shortened and the number
of common stock purchasable upon exercise of a warrant could be decreased, all without the approval of all securityholders.
peer_risks.name: Amendment of public warrants with 65% holder approval
peer_risks.why: The warrant agreement permits amendments adverse to holders if approved by at least 65% of outstanding public warrants, without needing all securityholder approval, as detailed in paragraphs [2] and [3].
peer_risks.description: The company can amend public warrant terms (e.g., increase exercise price, shorten period, reduce shares) with approval of 65% of holders, potentially harming other holders.

peer_risks.source_text:
We are an emerging
growth company within the meaning of the Securities Act, and if we take advantage of certain exemptions from disclosure requirements available
to emerging growth companies, this could make our securities less attractive to investors and may make it more difficult to compare our
performance with other public companies.
peer_risks.name: Reliance on emerging growth company exemptions
peer_risks.why: SpringBig is exempt from requirements like Section 404 auditor attestation, reduced executive compensation disclosures, and nonbinding advisory votes, which may cause investors to find securities less attractive, per paragraphs [4] and [5].
peer_risks.description: As an emerging growth company, SpringBig uses reduced disclosures, which may make securities less attractive and reduce investor confidence.

peer_risks.source_text:
Further, Section 102(b)(1)
of the JOBS Act exempts emerging growth companies from being required to comply with new or revised financial accounting standards until
private companies (that is, those that have not had a Securities Act registration statement declared effective or do not have a class
of securities registered under the Exchange Act) are required to comply with the new or revised financial accounting standards. The JOBS
Act provides that a company can elect to opt out of the extended transition period and comply with the requirements that apply to non-emerging
growth companies but any such an election to opt out is irrevocable. We have elected not to opt out of such extended transition period
which means that when a standard is issued or revised and it has different application dates for public or private companies, we, as an
emerging growth company, can adopt the new or revised standard at the time private companies adopt the new or revised standard. This may
make comparison of our financial statements with another public company which is neither an emerging growth company nor an emerging growth
company which has opted out of using the extended transition period difficult or impossible because of the potential differences in accountant
standards used.
peer_risks.name: Use of extended transition period for accounting standards
peer_risks.why: As an emerging growth company, SpringBig elected not to opt out of the extended transition period, meaning it follows private company timelines for new accounting standards, making financial statement comparisons difficult, as stated in paragraph [6].
peer_risks.description: SpringBig adopts new accounting standards at private company timelines, creating comparability issues with other public companies.

peer_risks.source_text:
As a public company, we have
and will continue to incur significant legal, accounting and other expenses that we did not incur as a private company, and these expenses
may increase even more after we are no longer an emerging growth company, as defined in Section 2(a) of the Securities Act. In addition,
we expect to record incremental share-based compensation expense in connection with the consummation of the business combination.
peer_risks.name: Increased costs as a public company
peer_risks.why: The company will incur significant legal, accounting, and other expenses as a public company, and these may increase after no longer being an emerging growth company, as defined in Section 2(a) of the Securities Act.
peer_risks.description: Operating as a public company incurs significant legal, accounting, and compliance expenses not experienced as a private company, which may increase further after losing emerging growth company status.

peer_risks.source_text:
We have and will continue
to incur increased costs as a result of operating as a public company and our management has and will continue to devote a substantial
amount of time to new compliance initiatives.
peer_risks.name: Increased time and resource burden on management
peer_risks.why: Management and other personnel have and will continue to devote a substantial amount of time to compliance initiatives under the Exchange Act, Sarbanes-Oxley Act, and Dodd-Frank Act.
peer_risks.description: Management and personnel must devote substantial time to complying with public company reporting and regulatory requirements, diverting focus from other business activities.

peer_risks.source_text:
As a public company, we are
subject to the reporting requirements of the Exchange Act, the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and the Dodd-Frank Act, as well as rules adopted, and
to be adopted, by the SEC. Our management and other personnel have and will continue to devote a substantial amount of time to these compliance
initiatives. Moreover, these rules and regulations have substantially increased our legal and financial compliance costs and made some
activities more time-consuming and costly. For example, these rules and regulations have made it more difficult and more expensive for
us to obtain director and officer liability insurance and forced us to accept reduced policy limits. We cannot predict or estimate the
amount or timing of additional costs we have and will continue to incur to respond to these requirements. The impact of these requirements
could also make it more difficult for us to attract and retain qualified persons to serve on our Board of Directors, our board committees
or as executive officers.
peer_risks.name: Higher legal and financial compliance costs
peer_risks.why: Rules under the Exchange Act, Sarbanes-Oxley Act, and Dodd-Frank Act have substantially increased legal and financial compliance costs and made activities more time-consuming and costly.
peer_risks.description: Compliance with public company regulations has substantially increased legal and financial costs and made activities more time-consuming and costly.

peer_risks.source_text:
As a public company, we are
subject to the reporting requirements of the Exchange Act, the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and the Dodd-Frank Act, as well as rules adopted, and
to be adopted, by the SEC. Our management and other personnel have and will continue to devote a substantial amount of time to these compliance
initiatives. Moreover, these rules and regulations have substantially increased our legal and financial compliance costs and made some
activities more time-consuming and costly. For example, these rules and regulations have made it more difficult and more expensive for
us to obtain director and officer liability insurance and forced us to accept reduced policy limits. We cannot predict or estimate the
amount or timing of additional costs we have and will continue to incur to respond to these requirements. The impact of these requirements
could also make it more difficult for us to attract and retain qualified persons to serve on our Board of Directors, our board committees
or as executive officers.
peer_risks.name: Reduced availability and higher cost of director and officer liability insurance
peer_risks.why: These rules and regulations have made it more difficult and more expensive to obtain director and officer liability insurance and forced the company to accept reduced policy limits.
peer_risks.description: Public company regulations have made it more difficult and expensive to obtain director and officer liability insurance, forcing reduced policy limits.

peer_risks.source_text:
As a public company, we are
subject to the reporting requirements of the Exchange Act, the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and the Dodd-Frank Act, as well as rules adopted, and
to be adopted, by the SEC. Our management and other personnel have and will continue to devote a substantial amount of time to these compliance
initiatives. Moreover, these rules and regulations have substantially increased our legal and financial compliance costs and made some
activities more time-consuming and costly. For example, these rules and regulations have made it more difficult and more expensive for
us to obtain director and officer liability insurance and forced us to accept reduced policy limits. We cannot predict or estimate the
amount or timing of additional costs we have and will continue to incur to respond to these requirements. The impact of these requirements
could also make it more difficult for us to attract and retain qualified persons to serve on our Board of Directors, our board committees
or as executive officers.
peer_risks.name: Difficulty attracting qualified board and executive personnel
peer_risks.why: The impact of these requirements could make it more difficult to attract and retain qualified persons to serve on the Board of Directors, board committees, or as executive officers.
peer_risks.description: Compliance burdens and regulatory risks may deter qualified individuals from serving on the Board or as executive officers.

peer_risks.source_text:
As a public company, we are
required to provide management’s attestation on internal controls as required under Section 404(a) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. The
standards required for a public company under Section 404(a) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act are significantly more stringent than those required
of us as a privately-held company. If we are not successful in implementing the additional requirements of Section 404(a) in a timely
manner or with adequate compliance, we may not be able to assess whether our internal controls over financial reporting are effective,
which may subject us to adverse regulatory consequences and could harm investor confidence and the market price of our securities.
peer_risks.name: Failure to implement Section 404(a) internal controls
peer_risks.why: If the company is not successful in implementing the additional requirements of Section 404(a) in a timely manner or with adequate compliance, it may not be able to assess whether internal controls over financial reporting are effective.
peer_risks.description: Failure to timely or adequately implement Section 404(a) internal controls may prevent an effective assessment of financial reporting controls.

peer_risks.source_text:
Failure to properly implement
internal controls on a timely basis may lead to the identification of one or more additional material weaknesses or control deficiencies
in the future, which may prevent us from being able to report our financial results accurately on a timely basis or help prevent fraud,
and could cause our reported financial results to be materially misstated and result in the loss of investor confidence or delisting and
cause the market price of our shares of common stock to decline. If we have additional material weaknesses in the future, it could affect
the financial results that we report or create a perception that those financial results do not fairly state our financial position or
results of operations. Either of those events could have an adverse effect on the value of our shares of common stock.
peer_risks.name: Material weaknesses in internal controls leading to misstated financials
peer_risks.why: Failure to properly implement internal controls on a timely basis may lead to the identification of one or more additional material weaknesses or control deficiencies, which may prevent accurate reporting or fraud prevention.
peer_risks.description: Failure to properly implement internal controls may result in material weaknesses that cause inaccurate financial reporting or prevent fraud detection.

peer_risks.source_text:
Further, even if we conclude
that our internal control over financial reporting provides reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and
the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with U.S. GAAP, because of its inherent limitations, internal
control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect fraud or misstatements. Failure to implement required new or improved controls,
or difficulties encountered in their implementation, could harm our results of operations or cause us to fail to meet our future reporting
obligations.
peer_risks.name: Inherent limitations of internal controls
peer_risks.why: Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect fraud or misstatements, even if concluded to provide reasonable assurance.
peer_risks.description: Even effective internal controls cannot prevent or detect all fraud or misstatements due to inherent limitations.

peer_risks.source_text:
We are subject to laws and
regulations enacted by national, regional and local governments. In particular, we will be required to comply with certain SEC and other
legal requirements. Compliance with, and monitoring of, applicable laws and regulations may be difficult, time consuming and costly. Those
laws and regulations and their interpretation and application may also change from time to time and those changes could have a material
adverse effect on our business, investments and results of operations. In addition, a failure to comply with applicable laws or regulations,
as interpreted and applied, could have a material adverse effect on our business and results of operations.
peer_risks.name: Non-compliance with governmental laws and regulations
peer_risks.why: Compliance with and monitoring of applicable laws and regulations may be difficult, time-consuming, and costly, and changes in their interpretation could have a material adverse effect.
peer_risks.description: Failure to comply with national, regional, or local laws and regulations, or changes in their interpretation, may materially harm business and operations.

peer_risks.source_text:
Anti-takeover provisions
in our certificate of incorporation and bylaws and under Delaware law could delay or prevent a change in control, limit the price investors
may be willing to pay in the future for our shares of common stock and could entrench management.
peer_risks.name: Anti-takeover provisions deterring acquisitions
peer_risks.why: Anti-takeover provisions in the certificate of incorporation and bylaws and under Delaware law could delay or prevent a change in control and limit the price investors may be willing to pay for shares.
peer_risks.description: Provisions in charter and bylaws under Delaware law may delay or prevent a change in control, limiting shareholder value potential.

peer_risks.source_text:
Our certificate of incorporation
and bylaws contain provisions that could make it more difficult for a third-party to acquire us without the consent of our Board of Directors.
These provisions provide for:
peer_risks.name: Board authority to issue preferred stock without shareholder approval
peer_risks.why: The Board of Directors has the ability to determine the powers, preferences, and rights of preference shares and to issue them without shareholder approval.
peer_risks.description: The Board can unilaterally determine and issue preferred stock with potentially dilutive or restrictive terms without shareholder consent.

peer_risks.source_text:
These provisions may make
more difficult the removal of management and may discourage transactions that otherwise could involve payment of a premium over prevailing
market prices for our securities. These provisions could also discourage proxy contests and make it more difficult shareholders to elect
directors of their choosing and cause us to take corporate actions other than those shareholders may desire, any of which could harm our
share price.
peer_risks.name: Provisions may make removal of management more difficult and discourage premium transactions
peer_risks.why: These provisions make it harder to remove management, discourage proxy contests, and prevent shareholders from electing preferred directors or triggering desired corporate actions, potentially harming share price.
peer_risks.description: Certain corporate provisions hinder removal of management, discourage premium-paying transactions, and impede shareholder efforts to elect directors or influence corporate actions.

peer_risks.source_text:
Our largest shareholders
and certain members of our management own a significant percentage of our shares of common stock and are able to exert significant control
over matters subject to shareholder approval.
peer_risks.name: Large shareholders and management exert significant control over shareholder-approved matters
peer_risks.why: They own a significant percentage of common stock, enabling them to influence matters like director elections, equity issuances, amendments to organizational documents, and major corporate transactions.
peer_risks.description: Large shareholders and management collectively own a significant percentage of shares and can exert substantial control over decisions requiring shareholder approval.

peer_risks.source_text:
Our founder and certain of
our largest shareholders hold a significant percentage of our shares of common stock. As a result, these holders have the ability to substantially
influence us and exert significant control through this ownership position and, in the case of certain holders, service on our Board of
Directors. For example, these holders may be able to control elections of directors, issuance of equity, including to our employees under
equity incentive plans, amendments of our organizational documents, or approval of any merger, amalgamation, sale of assets or other major
corporate transaction. These holders’ interests may not always coincide with our corporate interests or the interests of other shareholders,
and it may exercise its voting and other rights in a manner with which you may not agree or that may not be in the best interests of our
other shareholders. So long as these holders continue to own a significant amount of our equity, they will continue to be able to strongly
influence and effectively control our decisions.
peer_risks.name: Founder and large shareholders can substantially influence corporate decisions and may act contrary to other shareholders' interests
peer_risks.why: They hold a significant percentage of shares and serve on the Board, allowing them to control elections, equity issuances, amendments, mergers, or asset sales, with interests that may not align with other shareholders.
peer_risks.description: The founder and key shareholders, through ownership and board representation, can control key corporate decisions that may conflict with other shareholders' interests.

peer_risks.source_text:
Future sales and issuances
of our shares of common stock, including pursuant to our equity incentive and other compensatory plans, will result in additional dilution
of the percentage ownership of our shareholders and could cause our share price to fall.
peer_risks.name: Future issuances of common stock will dilute existing shareholders' ownership and may lower share price
peer_risks.why: Additional shares issued under equity incentive or compensatory plans reduce percentage ownership and may depress share price due to increased supply.
peer_risks.description: Future sales or issuances of common stock, including under equity incentive plans, will dilute ownership percentages and could cause share price declines.

peer_risks.source_text:
We may need additional capital
in the future to continue our planned operations. To the extent we raise additional capital by issuing equity securities, our shareholders
may experience substantial dilution. We may sell shares of common stock, convertible securities or other equity securities in one or more
transactions at prices and in a manner we determine from time to time. If we sell shares of common stock, convertible securities or other
equity securities in more than one transaction, investors may be materially diluted by subsequent sales. In addition, new investors could
gain rights superior to our existing shareholders.
peer_risks.name: Raising future capital through equity issuances may cause substantial dilution and grant superior rights to new investors
peer_risks.why: The company may issue shares or convertible securities at varying prices and terms, causing material dilution across multiple transactions and giving new investors rights superior to existing shareholders.
peer_risks.description: Future capital raises via equity or convertible securities may lead to significant shareholder dilution and grant new investors rights superior to existing ones.

peer_risks.source_text:
Pursuant to SpringBig Holdings,
Inc. 2022 Long-Term Incentive Plan (the “Incentive Plan”), we are authorized to grant options and other share-based awards
to our employees, directors and consultants. Shares subject to stock awards granted under the Incentive Plan that expire or terminate
without being exercised in full, or that are paid out in cash rather than in shares, will not reduce the number of shares available for
issuance under the Incentive Plan.
peer_risks.name: Unexercised or cash-paid awards under the Incentive Plan do not reduce available shares for issuance
peer_risks.why: The Incentive Plan allows grants of options and share-based awards where expired, terminated, or cash-paid awards do not reduce the total number of shares available for future issuance.
peer_risks.description: Shares underlying unexercised or cash-paid awards under the 2022 Incentive Plan do not count against the share reserve, enabling unlimited potential dilution.

peer_risks.source_text:
We have a relatively
short operating history in a rapidly evolving industry, which makes it difficult to evaluate our future prospects and may increase the
risk that we will not be successful. We may not be able to generate sufficient revenue to maintain profitability in the future.
peer_risks.name: Short operating history in a rapidly evolving industry
peer_risks.why: The company has a relatively short operating history in a quickly evolving industry with complex, conflicting regulations, making future success uncertain despite recent revenue growth.
peer_risks.description: Limited operating history and rapid changes in the cannabis industry make it difficult to evaluate future prospects and increase risk of failure.

peer_risks.source_text:
We have a relatively short
operating history in a quickly evolving industry that may not develop as we anticipate, if at all. Both our relatively short operating
history and the pace of dramatic change in the cannabis industry, and the complex, multiple and sometimes conflicting regulatory regimes
applicable to it, makes it difficult to assess our future prospects, and you should evaluate our business in light of the risks and difficulties
we may encounter as the industry continues to evolve. While our revenue has grown in recent periods, this growth may not be sustainable
due to a number of factors, including the maturation of our business, increased competition and the eventual decline in the number of
new major geographic markets in which the sale of cannabis is permitted and to which we have not already expanded. We may not be able
to generate sufficient revenue to achieve and sustain profitability.
peer_risks.name: Inability to achieve or sustain profitability
peer_risks.why: Revenue growth may not be sustainable due to business maturation, increased competition, and declining new geographic markets for cannabis sales.
peer_risks.description: The company may not generate sufficient revenue to maintain or achieve profitability in the future.

peer_risks.source_text:
Additionally, we may incur
increased expenditures which may not result in additional revenue or the growth of our business. If we fail to continue to grow revenue
or to sustain profitability, the market price of our securities could decline, and our business, operating results and financial condition
could be adversely affected.
peer_risks.name: Increased expenditures without corresponding revenue growth
peer_risks.why: Increased spending might not result in revenue growth or business expansion, potentially harming financial condition and market price of securities.
peer_risks.description: The company may incur higher expenditures that do not lead to additional revenue or business growth.

peer_risks.source_text:
If we do not successfully
develop and deploy new software, platform features or services to address the needs of our clients, our business, financial condition,
and results of operations could suffer.
peer_risks.name: Failure to develop or deploy new software or platform features
peer_risks.why: Clients demand evolving data analysis and integrations; failure to deliver compelling or timely enhancements risks losing market share and client retention.
peer_risks.description: Failure to create new software, features, or services to meet client needs could harm business, financial condition, and results of operations.

peer_risks.source_text:
Our success has been based
on our ability to design software, platform features and services that address the needs of our clients. We spend substantial amounts
of time and money researching and developing new technologies and enhanced versions of existing platform features, as well as new features,
to meet our clients’ rapidly evolving needs. As consumers and clients demand comprehensive data analysis from platforms such as
us, in conjunction with their point-of-sale providers, our ability to integrate with a client’s POS system and other third party
technology integrations may become increasingly important. If we are unable to arrange or complete new integrations, or improve our existing
integrations, we may lose market share to competitors. There is no assurance that enhancements to our software, platform features or new
services or capabilities will be compelling to our clients or gain market acceptance. If our research and development investments do not
accurately anticipate market demand or if we fail to develop our software, platform features or services in a manner that satisfies client
preferences in a timely and cost-effective manner, we may fail to retain our existing clients or increase demand for our services.
peer_risks.name: Inability to successfully integrate with third-party POS systems
peer_risks.why: Integration with client POS and third-party tech is increasingly important; inability to complete or improve integrations may cause clients to switch to competitors.
peer_risks.description: Failure to arrange or improve integrations with clients' point-of-sale systems could lead to loss of market share.

peer_risks.source_text:
The introduction of new products
and services by competitors or the development of entirely new technologies to replace existing service offerings could make our platforms
obsolete or adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. We may experience difficulties with software
development, design, or marketing that delay or prevent our development, introduction or implementation of new platforms, platform features
or capabilities, or cause errors to arise with our existing software. We have in the past experienced delays in our internally planned
release dates of new features and capabilities, and there can be no assurance that new platforms, platform features, or capabilities will
be released according to schedule. Any delays or other disruptions could result in adverse publicity, loss of revenue or market acceptance,
or claims by consumers or suppliers brought against us, any of which could harm our business. Moreover, the design and development of
new platforms or new platform features and capabilities to our existing platform may require substantial investment, and we have no assurance
that such investments will be successful. If consumers in the market do not widely adopt our new platforms, platform features, and capabilities,
we may not be able to realize a return on our investment and our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely
affected.
peer_risks.name: New competitor products or technologies rendering platforms obsolete
peer_risks.why: New competitor offerings or disruptive technologies could replace existing services, and delays in releasing new features may cause loss of revenue or market acceptance.
peer_risks.description: Competitors introducing new products or technologies could make SpringBig’s platforms obsolete or reduce demand.

peer_risks.source_text:
The introduction of new products
and services by competitors or the development of entirely new technologies to replace existing service offerings could make our platforms
obsolete or adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. We may experience difficulties with software
development, design, or marketing that delay or prevent our development, introduction or implementation of new platforms, platform features
or capabilities, or cause errors to arise with our existing software. We have in the past experienced delays in our internally planned
release dates of new features and capabilities, and there can be no assurance that new platforms, platform features, or capabilities will
be released according to schedule. Any delays or other disruptions could result in adverse publicity, loss of revenue or market acceptance,
or claims by consumers or suppliers brought against us, any of which could harm our business. Moreover, the design and development of
new platforms or new platform features and capabilities to our existing platform may require substantial investment, and we have no assurance
that such investments will be successful. If consumers in the market do not widely adopt our new platforms, platform features, and capabilities,
we may not be able to realize a return on our investment and our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely
affected.
peer_risks.name: Delays in releasing new software features or platforms
peer_risks.why: Past delays in planned feature releases have occurred, and future delays could trigger negative publicity, lost revenue, or claims from consumers or suppliers.
peer_risks.description: Delays in developing or launching new software features or platforms could cause adverse publicity, revenue loss, or legal claims.

peer_risks.source_text:
If we fail to retain
our existing clients and consumers or to acquire new clients and consumers in a cost-effective manner, our revenue may decrease, and our
business may be harmed.
peer_risks.name: Failure to retain existing or acquire new clients cost-effectively
peer_risks.why: Revenue depends on retaining existing clients and acquiring new ones efficiently; failure to do so directly threatens revenue streams and business viability.
peer_risks.description: Inability to retain current clients or acquire new ones in a cost-effective manner could reduce revenue and harm the business.

peer_risks.source_text:
We compete in a dynamic,
innovative, and fairly new market, which we expect will continue to evolve rapidly. We believe that our success is dependent on our ability
to continue identifying and anticipating the needs of our clients and, in turn, their consumers, and retaining our existing clients and
adding new clients. While we have historically been able to grow and retain our client base, we may grow more slowly than we expect or
than we have grown in the past. Our ability to retain clients depends in part on our ability to create and maintain high levels of client
satisfaction, which we may not always be capable of providing, including for reasons outside of our control. Any decrease in client satisfaction
or other change negatively affecting our ability to retain clients could result in a rapid, concentrated impact to our results going forward.
Therefore, our failure to retain existing clients, even if such losses are offset by an increase in revenue resulting from the acquisition
of new clients, could have an adverse effect on our business and operating results.
peer_risks.name: Failure to retain existing clients
peer_risks.why: The company's ability to retain clients depends on maintaining high satisfaction levels, which it may not always provide; any decrease could cause a rapid, concentrated adverse impact on results.
peer_risks.description: Loss of existing clients due to decreased satisfaction or uncontrollable factors could rapidly and negatively impact results, even if new clients are acquired.

peer_risks.source_text:
While a key part of our business
strategy is to add clients in our existing geographic markets, we intend to expand our operations into new markets if and as cannabis
continues to be legalized in new markets. Any such expansion places us in competitive markets with which we may be unfamiliar, requires
us to analyze the potential applicability of new and potentially complicated regulations regarding the usage, sale and marketing of cannabis,
and involves various risks, including the need to invest significant time and resources and the possibility that returns on such investments
will not be achieved for several years, if at all. As a result of such expansion, we may incur losses or otherwise fail to enter new markets
successfully. In attempting to establish a presence in new markets, we expect to incur significant expenses and face various other challenges,
such as expanding our compliance efforts to cover those new markets. These efforts may prove more expensive than we currently anticipate,
and we may not succeed in increasing our revenues sufficiently to offset these expenses. Our current and any future expansion plans will
require significant resources and management attention.
peer_risks.name: Expansion into new cannabis markets
peer_risks.why: Expansion requires investing significant time and resources, analyzing complex cannabis regulations, and may not yield returns for years, if at all, potentially leading to losses.
peer_risks.description: Expanding into new geographic markets with unfamiliar regulations and high costs risks significant expenses without guaranteed returns.

peer_risks.source_text:
We have a significant
working capital deficiency and a history of losses, may need to raise additional funds to meet our obligations and sustain our operations
and may not achieve profitability in the future.
peer_risks.name: Working capital deficiency and history of losses
peer_risks.why: As of December 31, 2024, SpringBig had a $1.5 million working capital deficiency and incurred net losses of $1.6 million in 2024 and $10.2 million in 2023.
peer_risks.description: The company has a working capital deficiency and a history of net losses, raising doubt about its ability to sustain operations without additional funding.

peer_risks.source_text:
SpringBig is an early-stage
company with a history of losses. We incurred net losses of $1.6 million and $10.2 million for the years ended December 31,
2024 and December 31, 2023, respectively. In addition, as of December 31, 2024, we had a working capital deficiency of $1.5 million
and we may need to raise additional funds to meet our obligations and sustain our operations. SpringBig may not achieve or maintain profitability
in the future. We may incur net losses in the future, and such losses may fluctuate significantly from quarter to quarter.
peer_risks.name: Inability to achieve or maintain profitability
peer_risks.why: SpringBig incurred net losses in 2023 and 2024, may need additional funds to sustain operations, and expects future losses that may fluctuate significantly quarter to quarter.
peer_risks.description: The company may not achieve or maintain profitability due to ongoing losses, fluctuating quarterly results, and high growth costs.

peer_risks.source_text:
Our efforts to grow our business
may be more costly than we expect, and we may not be able to increase our revenue sufficiently to offset our higher operating expenses.
We may incur significant losses, and we may not achieve or maintain future profitability, due to a number of reasons, including the risks
described in this report, unforeseen expenses, difficulties, complications and delays, and other unknown events. Furthermore, if our future
growth and operating performance fail to meet investor or analyst expectations, or if we have future negative cash flow or losses resulting
from our investment in acquiring customers or expanding our operations, this could make it difficult for you to evaluate our current business
and our future prospects and may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
peer_risks.name: Higher-than-expected growth costs
peer_risks.why: The company may incur significant losses due to unforeseen expenses, difficulties, delays, and investments in acquiring customers or expanding operations without sufficient revenue growth.
peer_risks.description: Growth initiatives may incur costs exceeding expectations, with insufficient revenue to offset them, leading to continued losses.

peer_risks.source_text:
Federal law enforcement
may deem our clients to be in violation of U.S. federal law, and, in particular the CSA. A change in U.S. federal policy on cannabis enforcement
and strict enforcement of federal cannabis laws against our clients would undermine our business model and materially affect our business
and operations.
peer_risks.name: Federal enforcement of cannabis laws against clients
peer_risks.why: Federal law enforcement may deem clients in violation of the CSA, leading to criminal actions, fines, forfeiture, or cessation of business activities that materially affect SpringBig.
peer_risks.description: Federal enforcement against clients under the CSA could undermine SpringBig’s business model by disrupting client operations.

peer_risks.source_text:
U.S. federal law, and more
specifically the CSA, proscribes the cultivation, processing, distribution, sale, advertisement and possession of cannabis. As a result,
U.S. federal law enforcement authorities, in their attempt to regulate the illegal or unauthorized production, distribution, promotion,
sale, possession, or use of cannabis, may seek to bring criminal actions against our clients under the CSA. If our clients are found to
be violating U.S. federal law relating to cannabis, they may be subject not only to criminal charges and convictions, but also to forfeiture
of property, significant fines and penalties, disgorgement of profits, administrative sanctions, cessation of business activities, or
civil liabilities arising from proceedings initiated by either the U.S. government or private citizens. Any of these actions or consequences
on our clients could have a material adverse effect on our business, operating results or financial condition, or could force us to cease
operations, and as a result, our investors could lose their entire investment.
peer_risks.name: Legal consequences to clients under the CSA
peer_risks.why: If clients are found violating federal cannabis laws, they may face criminal charges, forfeiture, fines, disgorgement, or civil liabilities, which could force SpringBig to cease operations.
peer_risks.description: Clients facing criminal or civil penalties under the CSA due to cannabis-related violations could force SpringBig to cease operations.

peer_risks.source_text:
Further, to the extent any
law enforcement actions require us to respond to subpoenas, or undergo search warrants, for client records, cannabis businesses could
elect to cease using our products and services. Until the U.S. federal government changes the laws with respect to cannabis, described
below under the caption “Cannabis remains illegal under federal law, and therefore, strict enforcement of federal laws regarding
cannabis would likely result in our inability to execute our business plan,” to apply to all state cannabis programs, U.S. federal
authorities could more strictly enforce current federal prohibitions and restrictions. An increase in federal enforcement against companies
licensed under state cannabis laws could negatively impact the state cannabis industries and, in turn, our business, operating results,
financial condition, brand and reputation.
peer_risks.name: Law enforcement actions against clients may cause them to cease using our products and services
peer_risks.why: The paragraph states that to the extent law enforcement actions require responding to subpoenas or search warrants for client records, cannabis businesses could elect to cease using the company's products and services.
peer_risks.description: If law enforcement subpoenas or search warrants target client records, cannabis businesses may stop using SpringBig's services.

peer_risks.source_text:

law enforcement actions require us to respond to subpoenas, or undergo search warrants, for client records, cannabis businesses could
elect to cease using our products and services. Until the U.S. federal government changes the laws with respect to cannabis, described
below under the caption “Cannabis remains illegal under federal law, and therefore, strict enforcement of federal laws regarding
cannabis would likely result in our inability to execute our business plan,” to apply to all state cannabis programs, U.S. federal
authorities could more strictly enforce current federal prohibitions and restrictions. An increase in federal enforcement against companies
licensed under state cannabis laws could negatively impact the state cannabis industries and, in turn, our business, operating results,
financial condition, brand and reputation.
peer_risks.name: Increased federal enforcement against state-licensed cannabis businesses could negatively impact our business
peer_risks.why: The paragraph warns that if federal authorities more strictly enforce current federal prohibitions against companies licensed under state cannabis laws, it could negatively impact the state cannabis industries and SpringBig's business, operating results, financial condition, brand, and reputation.
peer_risks.description: Stricter federal enforcement of cannabis prohibitions could harm state cannabis industries and, in turn, SpringBig's operations and reputation.

peer_risks.source_text:
Some of our clients
currently and in the future may not be in compliance with licensing and related requirements under applicable laws and regulations. Allowing
unlicensed or noncompliant businesses to access our platform and services, or allowing businesses to use our solutions in a noncompliant
manner, may subject us to legal or regulatory enforcement and negative publicity, which could adversely impact our business, operating
results, financial condition, brand and reputation. In addition, allowing businesses that engage in false or deceptive advertising practices
to use our solutions may subject us to negative publicity, which could have similar adverse impacts on us.
peer_risks.name: Clients may be unlicensed or noncompliant with state cannabis laws, exposing us to enforcement and negative publicity
peer_risks.why: The paragraph states that allowing unlicensed or noncompliant businesses to access our platform or use our solutions in a noncompliant manner may subject us to legal or regulatory enforcement and negative publicity.
peer_risks.description: Allowing unlicensed or noncompliant cannabis businesses to use our platform may subject us to legal enforcement and reputational harm.

peer_risks.source_text:
Some of our clients
currently and in the future may not be in compliance with licensing and related requirements under applicable laws and regulations. Allowing
unlicensed or noncompliant businesses to access our platform and services, or allowing businesses to use our solutions in a noncompliant
manner, may subject us to legal or regulatory enforcement and negative publicity, which could adversely impact our business, operating
results, financial condition, brand and reputation. In addition, allowing businesses that engage in false or deceptive advertising practices
to use our solutions may subject us to negative publicity, which could have similar adverse impacts on us.
peer_risks.name: Clients using our platform for false or deceptive advertising may subject us to negative publicity
peer_risks.why: The paragraph explicitly states that allowing businesses that engage in false or deceptive advertising practices to use our solutions may subject us to negative publicity with adverse impacts.
peer_risks.description: If clients use our solutions to engage in false or deceptive advertising, we may face reputational damage.

peer_risks.source_text:
Any legal or regulatory enforcement
against us based on our platform, the content provided by clients, the marketing campaigns created by clients on our platform or noncompliance
by our clients with licensing and other legal requirements, could subject us to various risks, including monetary penalties and/or required
changes to our platform or business model, and would likely cause us to experience negative publicity. Any of these developments could
materially and adversely impact our business, operating results, financial condition, brand, and reputation.
peer_risks.name: Legal enforcement actions against us due to client noncompliance may result in penalties or business model changes
peer_risks.why: The paragraph states that any legal or regulatory enforcement against us based on client noncompliance could subject us to monetary penalties and/or required changes to our platform or business model.
peer_risks.description: Enforcement against us for client noncompliance with licensing or legal requirements could lead to penalties or required changes to our platform.

peer_risks.source_text:
We generally do not,
and cannot, ensure that our clients will conduct their business activities in a manner compliant with the complex, disparate and constantly
evolving regulations and requirements affecting the legal cannabis industry. As a result, federal, state, provincial or local government
authorities may seek to bring criminal, administrative or regulatory enforcement actions against our clients, which could have a material
adverse effect on our business, operating results or financial conditions, or could force us to cease operations.
peer_risks.name: We cannot ensure client compliance with complex, evolving cannabis regulations, exposing us to enforcement actions
peer_risks.why: The paragraph states we generally do not and cannot ensure clients comply with complex, disparate, and constantly evolving regulations, and government authorities may bring enforcement actions against our clients, which could materially affect our business or force us to cease operations.
peer_risks.description: Due to the complexity and constant evolution of cannabis regulations, we cannot ensure client compliance, risking government enforcement against us.

peer_risks.source_text:
While our solutions provide
features to support our clients’ compliance with certain regulations and other legal requirements applicable to the cannabis industry,
and we have policies and procedures regarding the verification and periodic screening of the licensing status of our clients, we generally
do not, and cannot, ensure that at all times our clients will conduct their business activities in a manner compliant with such regulations
and requirements, in whole or in part. Their legal noncompliance could result in regulatory and even criminal actions against them, which
could lead to a material adverse impact on our business and operating results or financial condition, and as a result, our investors could
lose their entire investment. For additional information, see the other risk factors in this section, including “Some of our clients
currently and in the future may not be in compliance with licensing and related requirements under applicable laws and regulations. Allowing
unlicensed or noncompliant businesses to access our platform and services, or allowing businesses to use our solutions in a noncompliant
manner, may subject us to legal or regulatory enforcement and negative publicity, which could adversely impact our business, operating
results, financial condition, brand and reputation. In addition, allowing businesses that engage in false or deceptive advertising practices
to use our solutions may subject us to negative publicity, which could have similar adverse impacts on us.”
peer_risks.name: Client noncompliance with cannabis regulations may lead to regulatory or criminal actions that harm our business or cause investor losses
peer_risks.why: The paragraph states that client legal noncompliance could result in regulatory and even criminal actions against them, which could lead to a material adverse impact on our business and operating results or financial condition, and investors could lose their entire investment.
peer_risks.description: Client legal noncompliance may trigger regulatory or criminal actions against them, which could materially harm our business and cause investors to lose their investment.
